For your stir-fry, a good alternative to soy sauce that provides a similar savory, umami flavor is coconut aminos. It is made from the sap of coconut blossoms and salt, making it soy-free and generally safer for those with soy allergies. It has a slightly sweeter and less salty profile than soy sauce, so you may want to adjust the seasoning accordingly. Another option is tamari if the allergy is strictly to soy protein but not gluten, but since the allergy is to soy, coconut aminos is the safer bet. You can also use a mixture of beef or mushroom broth with a dash of balsamic vinegar or molasses to mimic the depth of flavor.
